answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Because the hollow fee is applied at the haven exit, the vertex audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 13% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
